event-title.$: ENTRY INTO FORCE OF REQUEST FOR SUBSTANTIVE EXAMINATION

section.content: The invention provides a machine learning device capable of efficiently learning a neural network model in a vehicle. The machine learning device provided in a vehicle is provided with: a learning planning unit (81) that creates a learning plan for the neural network model; a data set creation unit (82) that obtains actual measurement values of a plurality of input parameters and actual measurement values of at least one output parameter, and creates a training data set; a learning unit (83) that performs learning of the neural network model when the vehicle is stationary; and a parking period prediction unit (84) that predicts a parking period of the vehicle. The data set creating unit divides the training data set into a plurality of learning regions defined based on the respective ranges of the plurality of input parameters. The learning unit learns the neural network model for each learning region. The learning planning unit allocates a plurality of learning regions to the parking period so that learning of the neural network model is not interrupted during the parking period.

本发明提供一种能够在车辆中高效地进行神经网络模型的学习的机器学习装置。设于车辆的机器学习装置具备：学习计划部(81)，其制作神经网络模型的学习计划；数据集制作部(82)，其取得多个输入参数的实测值和至少一个输出参数的实测值来制作训练数据集；学习部(83)，其在车辆停着时进行神经网络模型的学习；以及停车期间预测部(84)，其预测车辆的停车期间。数据集制作部将训练数据集分到基于多个输入参数的各个范围确定的多个学习区域。学习部按各学习区域进行神经网络模型的学习。学习计划部将多个学习区域分配到停车期间以使得在停车期间中神经网络模型的学习不中断。

Machine learning deviceTechnical Field

The present invention relates to a machine learning device.

Background

Conventionally, it has been known to calculate a predetermined output parameter from a predetermined input parameter using a neural network model including an input layer, a hidden layer, and an output layer. For example, in the control device for an internal combustion engine described in patent document 1, the flow rate of intake air to be taken into the combustion chamber of the internal combustion engine is estimated using a learned neural network model.

Prior art literature

Patent document 1: japanese patent application laid-open No. 2012-112277

Disclosure of Invention

Technical problem to be solved by the invention

However, in the case where the learned neural network model is applied to a vehicle, there are cases where the characteristics of the vehicle change due to aged deterioration or the like. In this case, the correspondence relation between the input parameter and the output parameter changes, and the accuracy of calculating the output parameter based on the neural network model decreases. In addition, the characteristics of the vehicle vary somewhat from vehicle to vehicle.

Therefore, in order to improve the accuracy of calculating the output parameters, it is considered to acquire a training data set for learning in the vehicle and learn the neural network model in the vehicle. However, in a control device that can be used for learning, it is necessary to control a driving source (an internal combustion engine, an electric motor, etc.) of the vehicle during running of the vehicle. Therefore, it is difficult to perform learning with high calculation load during the running of the vehicle.

Then, learning of the neural network model is considered to be performed while the vehicle is stationary. However, in the case where the learning time is longer than the parking period, the learning cannot be completed during the parking period. As a result, the neural network model may not be updated at an appropriate frequency, and the accuracy of calculation of the output parameters based on the neural network model may be deteriorated.

In view of the above, an object of the present invention is to provide a machine learning device capable of efficiently learning a neural network model in a vehicle.

Technical scheme for solving problems

The gist of the present disclosure is as follows.

(1) A machine learning device provided in a vehicle is provided with: a learning plan unit that creates a learning plan of a neural network model that outputs at least one output parameter from a plurality of input parameters; a data set creating unit that creates a training data set by acquiring actual measurement values of the plurality of input parameters and actual measurement values of the at least one output parameter corresponding to the actual measurement values; a learning unit that performs learning of the neural network model using the training data set when the vehicle is stationary, based on the learning plan; and a parking period prediction unit that predicts a parking period of the vehicle, wherein the data set creation unit divides the training data set into a plurality of learning regions determined based on respective ranges of the plurality of input parameters, the learning unit performs learning of the neural network model for each learning region, and the learning planning unit assigns the plurality of learning regions to the parking period so that learning of the neural network model is not interrupted during the parking period.

(2) The machine learning device according to the above (1), wherein the plurality of learning regions include a small learning region and a large learning region including the small learning region, the small learning region and the large learning region are set such that a data density of the small learning region is higher than a data density of the large learning region, and the learning planning unit selectively assigns the small learning region and the large learning region to the parking period.

(3) The machine learning device according to the above (1), wherein a priority of learning is given to the plurality of learning regions.

(4) According to the machine learning device described in (3), the learning planning unit sets a higher priority for learning a learning region including a value of the input parameter having a relatively high frequency of occurrence than for learning a learning region including a value of the input parameter having a relatively low frequency of occurrence.

(5) According to the machine learning device described in the above (3), the learning planning unit changes the priority of the learning according to information on a road on which the vehicle is traveling or a warm-up state of an internal combustion engine provided in the vehicle.

ADVANTAGEOUS EFFECTS OF INVENTION

According to the present invention, a machine learning device capable of efficiently learning a neural network model in a vehicle can be provided.

Detailed Description

Hereinafter, embodiments of the present invention will be described in detail with reference to the accompanying drawings. In the following description, the same reference numerals are given to the same constituent elements.

< first embodiment >, first embodiment

First, a first embodiment of the present invention will be described with reference to fig. 1 to 10.

< description of the internal Combustion Engine as a whole >, and

fig. 1 is a diagram schematically showing an internal combustion engine to which the machine learning device according to the first embodiment is applied. The internal combustion engine 1 is a spark ignition type internal combustion engine (for example, a gasoline engine) that ignites a mixture gas by a spark plug, and is provided in a vehicle.

The internal combustion engine 1 includes an engine main body 3. The engine body 3 includes a cylinder block in which a plurality of cylinders 2 are formed, a cylinder head in which an intake port and an exhaust port are formed, and a crankcase. The cylinder head is provided with an intake valve configured to open and close an intake port, an exhaust valve configured to open and close an exhaust port, a fuel injection valve configured to directly inject fuel into a combustion chamber, and a spark plug configured to generate spark.

In the present embodiment, the number of cylinders 2 is four. An intake manifold 4 and an exhaust manifold 5 are connected to each cylinder 2.

The intake manifold 4 is connected to an outlet of a compressor 7a of the turbocharger 7 via an intake pipe 6. An inlet of the compressor 7a is connected to an air cleaner 8 via an intake pipe 6. A throttle valve 9 driven by a throttle valve drive actuator is disposed in the intake pipe 6. Further, an intercooler 13 for cooling intake air flowing in the intake pipe 6 is disposed around the intake pipe 6. The intercooler 13 may be incorporated in the intake manifold 4. The intake manifold 4 and the intake pipe 6 form an intake passage that guides air into the cylinders 2.

On the other hand, the exhaust manifold 5 is connected to an inlet of the turbine 7b of the turbocharger 7 via an exhaust pipe 27. The outlet of the turbine 7b is connected to a catalyst 29 via an exhaust pipe 27. The catalyst 29 is, for example, a three-way catalyst that purifies HC, CO, NOx and the like in exhaust gas. The exhaust manifold 5 and the exhaust pipe 27 form an exhaust passage through which exhaust gas generated by combustion of the mixture is discharged from the cylinders 2.

The exhaust passage and the intake passage are connected to each other via an exhaust gas recirculation passage (EGR passage, exhaust gas recirculation passage) 14. The EGR passage 14 recirculates a part of the exhaust gas flowing through the exhaust passage as EGR gas to the intake passage. In addition, an electronically controlled EGR control valve 15 is provided in the EGR passage 14. The EGR control valve 15 adjusts the amount of EGR gas that flows back from the exhaust passage to the intake passage. Further, an EGR cooler 16 for cooling the EGR gas is provided in the EGR passage 14.

In the present embodiment, the EGR passage 14 is connected to an exhaust passage downstream of the catalyst 29 and an intake passage upstream of the compressor 7 a. Therefore, the internal combustion engine 1 is provided with an EGR system of a so-called low pressure circulation system (LPL system). The internal combustion engine 1 may be provided with another EGR system. For example, the internal combustion engine 1 may be provided with an EGR system of a so-called high pressure cycle system (HPL system). In this case, the EGR passage is connected to, for example, the exhaust manifold 5 and the intake manifold 4.

The configuration of the internal combustion engine 1 is not limited to the above configuration. Therefore, the specific configuration of the internal combustion engine such as the cylinder arrangement, the fuel injection system, the configuration of the intake and exhaust systems, the configuration of the valve operating mechanism, the configuration of the supercharger, and the presence or absence of the supercharger may be different from that shown in fig. 1. For example, the fuel injection valve may also be configured to inject fuel into the intake port.

< constitution of ECU >

An Electronic Control Unit (ECU) is provided in a vehicle on which the internal combustion engine 1 is mounted. Fig. 2 is a diagram schematically showing the configuration of the ECU. The ECU60 includes a communication interface 61, a memory 62, and a processor 63, and executes various controls of the vehicle. For example, various controls of the internal combustion engine 1 are executed by the ECU60 based on outputs of various sensors and the like. In the present embodiment, one ECU60 is provided, but a plurality of ECUs may be provided for each function.

The communication interface 61 has an interface circuit for connecting the ECU60 to an in-vehicle network in accordance with a standard such as CAN (Controller Area Network ) or the like. The ECU60 communicates with other in-vehicle devices via the communication interface 61.

The memory 62 has, for example, a volatile semiconductor memory (e.g., RAM) and a nonvolatile semiconductor memory (e.g., ROM). The memory 62 stores programs executed in the processor 63, various data used when various processes are executed by the processor 63, and the like.

The processor 63 has one or more CPUs (Central Processing Unit, central processing units) and peripheral circuits thereof, and executes various processes. The processor 63 may further include an arithmetic circuit such as a logic arithmetic unit or a numerical arithmetic unit. The communication interface 61, the memory 62, and the processor 63 are connected to each other via signal lines.

The ECU60 is connected to the actuator 91 via an in-vehicle network, and controls the actuator 91. In the present embodiment, the actuator 91 includes a fuel injection valve, a spark plug, a throttle valve drive actuator, an EGR control valve 15, and the like.

In addition, a GPS receiver 92 is provided in the vehicle. The GPS receiver 92 receives signals from three or more GPS satellites and detects the current position of the vehicle (e.g., the latitude and longitude of the vehicle). The GPS receiver 92 is connected to the ECU60 via an in-vehicle network, and the output of the GPS receiver 92 is transmitted to the ECU60.

The vehicle is provided with a map database 93. The map database 93 stores map information. The map information includes road information such as position information of a road, shape information of a road (for example, types of curves and straight portions, a radius of curvature of a curve, a road gradient, and the like), road types, and a vehicle speed limit. The map database 93 is connected to the ECU60 via an in-vehicle network, and the ECU60 acquires map information from the map database 93.

In addition, a navigation system 94 is provided in the vehicle. The navigation system 94 sets a travel path to the vehicle at the destination based on the current position of the vehicle detected by the GPS receiver 92, map information of the map database 93, an input of the driver of the vehicle, and the like. The navigation system 94 is connected to the ECU60 via an in-vehicle network, and the travel path set by the navigation system 94 is transmitted to the ECU60. The GPS receiver 92 and the map database 93 may be incorporated in the navigation system 94.

The vehicle is provided with a communication module 95. The communication module 95 is a device capable of achieving communication between the vehicle and the outside of the vehicle. The communication module 95 includes, for example, a data communication module (DCM (Data communication module)), a short-range wireless communication module, and the like. The vehicle communicates with a server or the like outside the vehicle via a data communication module. In addition, the vehicle communicates with the roadside machine through road-to-vehicle communication via the short-range wireless module, and communicates with the vehicle through vehicle-to-vehicle communication. The information received by the communication module 95 is sent to the ECU60.

The outputs of an airflow meter 71, an air-fuel ratio sensor 72, a NOx sensor 73, a crank angle sensor 74, a load sensor 75, a torque sensor 76, and a vehicle speed sensor 77 are input to the ECU60.

The airflow meter 71 detects the flow rate of air in the intake passage. As shown in fig. 1, an air flow meter 71 is disposed in the intake pipe 6 between the air cleaner 8 and the compressor 7 a. The air flow meter 71 is electrically connected to the ECU60, and the output of the air flow meter 71 is sent to the ECU60.

The air-fuel ratio sensor 72 detects the air-fuel ratio of the exhaust gas. As shown in fig. 1, the air-fuel ratio sensor 72 is disposed in the exhaust pipe 27 between the turbine 7b and the catalyst 29. The air-fuel ratio sensor 72 is electrically connected to the ECU60, and the output of the air-fuel ratio sensor 72 is sent to the ECU60.

The NOx sensor 73 detects the concentration of nitrogen oxides (NOx) in the exhaust gas. As shown in fig. 1, the NOx sensor 73 is disposed in the exhaust pipe 27 between the turbine 7b and the catalyst 29. The NOx sensor 73 is electrically connected to the ECU60, and the output of the NOx sensor 73 is sent to the ECU60.

The crank angle sensor 74 generates an output pulse every time the crankshaft of the internal combustion engine 1 rotates by a predetermined angle (for example, 10 degrees). Crank angle sensor 74 is electrically connected to ECU60, and the output of crank angle sensor 74 is sent to ECU60. The ECU60 calculates the engine rotational speed based on the output of the crank angle sensor 74.

The load sensor 75 is connected to an accelerator pedal provided in the vehicle, and detects the amount of depression of the accelerator pedal. The load sensor 75 is electrically connected to the ECU60, and an output of the load sensor 75 is sent to the ECU60. The ECU60 calculates the engine load based on the output of the load sensor 75.

The torque sensor 76 is disposed, for example, on a crankshaft of the internal combustion engine 1, and detects the output torque of the internal combustion engine 1. The torque sensor 76 is electrically connected to the ECU60, and the output of the torque sensor 76 is sent to the ECU60.

The vehicle speed sensor 77 is provided in the vehicle and detects the speed of the vehicle. The vehicle speed sensor 77 is electrically connected to the ECU60, and an output of the vehicle speed sensor 77 is sent to the ECU60.

In the present embodiment, the ECU60 also functions as a machine learning device provided in the vehicle to learn the neural network model.

< learning of neural network model in vehicle >)

In the present embodiment, the neural network model as shown in fig. 3 is actually mounted on a vehicle (specifically, ECU 60). In the present embodiment, the object of the neural network model is the internal combustion engine 1. Accordingly, the neural network model outputs at least one output parameter of the internal combustion engine 1 according to a plurality of input parameters of the internal combustion engine 1.

The neural network model is learned (i.e., the weights w and the offsets b are set) before the vehicle leaves the factory. In learning the neural network model, a training data set including a combination of an actual measurement value of an input parameter and an actual measurement value of an output parameter corresponding to the actual measurement value of the input parameter is used. Specifically, the values of the weight w and the bias b in the neural network model are repeatedly updated by the error back propagation method described above using a large number of training data sets. As a result, the neural network model is learned, and the learned neural network model is created.

However, the actual internal combustion engine 1 provided in the vehicle on which the neural network model is actually mounted is not used for a large number of training data sets, but is acquired in advance by using an internal combustion engine for training data preparation such as an engine block. In addition, the characteristics of the internal combustion engine 1 may be somewhat different from those of the internal combustion engine for training data generation. Therefore, there is a possibility that the learned neural network model does not exactly coincide with the characteristics of the internal combustion engine 1. Further, the characteristics of the internal combustion engine 1 may also change due to aged deterioration or the like.

Therefore, in the present embodiment, in order to improve the accuracy of the output parameters calculated by the neural network model, the ECU60 is also used to learn the neural network model in the vehicle. Thus, the neural network model can accurately match the characteristics of the internal combustion engine 1, and the accuracy of the output parameters calculated by the neural network model can be improved.

Fig. 4 is a functional block diagram of the ECU 60. In the present embodiment, ECU60 includes a learning planning unit 81, a data set creating unit 82, a learning unit 83, a parking period predicting unit 84, an arithmetic unit 85, and a control unit 86. These are functional blocks realized by processor 63 of ECU60 executing programs stored in memory 62 of ECU 60.

The learning planning unit 81 creates a learning plan of a neural network model that outputs at least one output parameter from a plurality of input parameters. The data set creating unit 82 obtains actual measurement values of a plurality of input parameters and actual measurement values of output parameters corresponding to the actual measurement values, and creates a training data set. The training data set includes a combination of measured values of a plurality of input parameters and measured values of output parameters corresponding to the measured values. The learning unit 83 performs learning of the neural network model using the training data set acquired in the vehicle by the data set creating unit 82 based on the learning plan created by the learning planning unit 81.

The neural network model is stored in a memory 62 of the ECU 60. The neural network model has, for example, the configuration shown in fig. 3. The number of layers of the neural network model may be any number of three or more layers. The number of nodes in the input layer may be any number of two or more. The number of nodes in each hidden layer and output layer may be any number of one or more.

The parking period predicting unit 84 predicts a parking period (hereinafter, simply referred to as "parking period") of the vehicle. Specifically, the parking period predicting unit 84 predicts a date and time (parking date and time) at which the parking period is generated and a time length (parking time) of the parking period. The parking of the vehicle means a state in which the vehicle speed is zero. Therefore, parking of the vehicle includes a state in which the vehicle is temporarily stopped before a traffic light, a state in which the vehicle is temporarily stopped due to congestion, a state in which the vehicle is parked in a parking lot such as a home, and the like.

In the case of using a vehicle for use in commute, school, shopping, and the like, the period of time in which the vehicle is used is often substantially constant. Therefore, the parking period prediction unit 84 predicts the parking period based on, for example, the travel history information of the vehicle. In this case, the travel history information of the vehicle in the past predetermined period is stored in, for example, the memory 62 of the ECU 60. The travel history information of the vehicle may be stored in another storage device provided in the vehicle.

The travel history information includes date, day of week, time period, weather, position of the vehicle, presence or absence of travel of the vehicle, and the like. In the case where the vehicle is provided with a driver monitoring camera that captures an image of a driver of the vehicle, the travel history information may include driver information. In this case, the driver of the vehicle is determined by the driver monitoring camera in order to predict the parking period, and thus, even when the vehicle is used by a plurality of persons, the prediction accuracy during parking can be improved.

The parking period prediction unit 84 may predict the parking period based on the current position of the vehicle detected by the GPS receiver 92, the travel path of the vehicle set by the navigation system 94, and the like. The parking period prediction unit 84 may predict the parking period based on information (traffic signal information, congestion information, weather information, etc.) received by the communication module 95 from the server, the roadside machine, or another vehicle. The parking period prediction unit 84 may predict the parking period by combining the above-described prediction methods.

The parking period prediction unit 84 predicts a parking period in a predetermined period in the future. Fig. 5 is a diagram showing an example of a prediction result during a parking period. In this example, the parking period predicting unit 84 predicts the parking period of the vehicle during the period of three days (8 months 9 days to 8 months 11 days) in the future. Fig. 5 shows a driving period predicted to drive the vehicle and a parking period predicted to stop the vehicle (hatched portion). The width of the travel period indicates the time length of the travel period, and the width of the parking period indicates the time length of the parking period. The successive parking periods are given respective parking period numbers (p=1 to 7).

The ECU60 also functions as a control device for the internal combustion engine 1. Therefore, the ECU60 controls the internal combustion engine 1 in order to obtain power for running when the vehicle is running. Therefore, the calculation resources of the ECU60 that can be used for learning the neural network model are limited. However, in learning the neural network model, many operations are required to update the weights w and the offsets b. Therefore, it is difficult to perform learning with a high calculation load during running of the vehicle by the ECU 60. In addition, increasing the processing capability of the ECU60 for learning during running of the vehicle or providing an additional ECU for learning increases the cost of the vehicle.

Then, in the present embodiment, the learning unit 83 learns the neural network model when the vehicle is stopped. This makes it possible to learn the neural network model when the computational resources of the ECU60 are free.

However, in the case where the learning time of the neural network model is longer than the parking period, the learning cannot be completed during the parking period. As a result, the neural network model may not be updated with an appropriate frequency, and the accuracy of calculation of the output parameters based on the neural network model may be deteriorated.

The greater the number of training data sets used for learning, the longer the learning time of the neural network model. Therefore, in order to shorten the learning time, it is necessary to reduce the number of training data sets used in one learning.

The plurality of input parameters of the neural network model have predetermined ranges, respectively. The predetermined range is set, for example, as a range between an upper limit value and a lower limit value of values that may occur in the internal combustion engine 1. When learning is performed using a training data set in the entire range of input parameters, a considerable time is required for learning, and the learning cannot be completed during the parking period.

In the present embodiment, the training data set created is divided into a plurality of learning regions, and the training data set in the learning region is used for each learning region to learn the neural network model. This can reduce the learning time per time, and can increase the update frequency of the neural network model. Therefore, the learning of the neural network model can be efficiently performed in the vehicle.

In order to perform the above-described processing, the data set creating unit 82 divides the training data set into a plurality of learning regions specified based on the respective ranges of the plurality of input parameters. Fig. 6 is a diagram schematically showing a plurality of learning regions in the first embodiment. In this example, as input parameters of the neural network model, two parameters (input parameter a and input parameter B) are used.

The input parameter a has a predetermined range, which is divided into a plurality of areas. Likewise, the input parameter B has a predetermined range, which is divided into a plurality of areas. In this example, in the input parameter a and the input parameter B, the divided regions have the same width.

The space defined by the input parameter a and the input parameter B (two-dimensional space in the example of fig. 6) is divided into a plurality of learning regions. Each learning region is delimited by a range of input parameters a and a range of input parameters B. Each learning region is assigned a learning region number (i=1 to n). In addition, the space defined by the plurality of input parameters and the dimension of the learning region are equal to the number of input parameters. The number of learning regions is a value obtained by multiplying the number of all regions of the plurality of input parameters.

The learning unit 83 learns the neural network model for each learning region. The learning planning section 81 allocates a plurality of learning regions to the parking period so that learning of the neural network model is not interrupted during the parking period. In other words, the learning planning section 81 allocates a plurality of learning regions to the parking period so that learning of the neural network model in each learning region is completed during the parking period. Thus, the neural network model in each learning region can be learned in a continuous parking period, and the frequency of updating the neural network model can be increased.

In the example of fig. 5, the 1 st learning region (i=1) is allocated to the 1 st parking period (p=1), the 2 nd learning region (i=2) is allocated to the 2 nd parking period (p=2), the 3 rd learning region (i=3) is allocated to the 3 rd parking period (p=3), the 4 th learning region (i=4) and the 5 th learning region (i=5) are allocated to the 4 th parking period (p=4), the 6 th learning region (i=1) to the 12 th learning region (i=12) are allocated to the 5 th parking period (p=5), the 13 th learning region (i=13) and the 14 th learning region (i=14) are allocated to the 6 th parking period (p=6), and the 15 th learning region (i=15) and the 16 th learning region (i=16) are allocated to the 7 th parking period (p=7).

The calculation unit 85 calculates the output parameters using the neural network model. Specifically, the arithmetic unit 85 inputs the input parameters to the neural network model, and causes the neural network model to output the output parameters. Thus, the output parameter corresponding to the input parameter can be predicted without detecting the actual measurement value of the output parameter by a sensor or the like.

The control unit 86 controls the vehicle based on the value of the output parameter calculated by the calculation unit 85. In the present embodiment, the control unit 86 controls the internal combustion engine 1 based on the value of the output parameter calculated by the calculation unit 85. For example, when the output parameter is the NOx concentration in the exhaust gas, the control unit 86 increases the opening degree of the EGR control valve 15 so that the NOx concentration is reduced when the predicted value of the NOx concentration calculated by the calculation unit 85 is higher than the target concentration.

Hereinafter, control for learning a neural network model in a vehicle will be described in detail with reference to flowcharts of fig. 7 to 10.

Data set creation process

Fig. 7 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the data set creating process in the first embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the ECU60 at predetermined time intervals.

First, in step S101, the data set creating unit 82 obtains actual measurement values of input parameters and actual measurement values of output parameters corresponding to the actual measurement values. The actual measurement values of the input parameter and the output parameter are values detected by a sensor or the like, and are calculated based on a command value output from the ECU60 to the actuator 91, and the like.

Next, in step S102, the data set creating unit 82 creates a training data set by combining the actual measurement value of the input parameter and the actual measurement value of the output parameter.

Next, in step S103, the data set creating unit 82 divides the training data set into learning regions. At this time, the training data set is divided into the learning region such that the actual measurement value of the input parameter of the training data set is included in the range of the input parameter that demarcates the learning region. The training data set is stored in the memory 62 of the ECU60 together with the learning region number i of the corresponding learning region. The training data sets stored in the memory 62 are deleted in order from the old data, and the latest predetermined number of training data sets are stored in the memory 62. The training data set may be stored in another storage device provided in the vehicle. After step S103, the present control routine ends.

< prediction processing during parking >)

Fig. 8 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the parking period prediction process in the first embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the ECU60 at predetermined time intervals.

First, in step S201, the parking period prediction unit 84 predicts the parking period using the prediction method described above. Next, in step S202, the parking period predicting unit 84 assigns a parking period number p to the parking period as shown in the example of fig. 5. After step S202, the present control routine ends.

< learning plan creation Process >)

Fig. 9 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the learning plan creation process in the first embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the ECU60 at predetermined time intervals.

First, in step S301, the learning planning unit 81 sets the learning area number i and the parking period number p to 1.

Next, in step S302, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not a training data set exists in the i-th learning region. When the training data set assigned to the i-th learning region is stored in the memory 62 of the ECU60, the learning planning unit 81 determines that the training data set is present in the i-th learning region. If it is determined in step S302 that the training data set exists in the i-th learning region, the present control routine proceeds to step S303.

In step S303, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the parking time STp during the p-th parking is equal to or longer than the learning time LTi of the i-th learning region. At this time, the learning planning unit 81 calculates the learning time LTi of the i-th learning region based on the number of training data sets assigned to the i-th learning region. The greater the number of training data sets, the longer the learning time LTi of the i-th learning region. On the other hand, the value predicted by the parking period predicting unit 84 may be used for the parking time STp in the p-th parking period.

If it is determined in step S303 that the parking time STp during the p-th parking period is equal to or longer than the learning time LTi of the i-th learning region, the control routine proceeds to step S304. In this case, learning of the neural network model in the i-th learning region can be completed in the p-th parking period. Therefore, in step S304, the learning planning section 81 allocates the i-th learning region to the p-th parking period.

Next, in step S305, the learning planning unit 81 updates the parking time STp in the p-th parking period in order to determine whether the next learning region can be divided into the p-th parking period. Specifically, the learning planning unit 81 sets a value obtained by subtracting the learning time LTi of the i-th learning region from the parking time STp during the p-th parking period as the new parking time STp.

After step S305, the present control routine advances to step S308. In addition, when it is determined in step S302 that the training data set does not exist in the i-th learning region, the present control routine also advances to step S308. In step S308, the learning planning unit 81 adds 1 to the learning region number i. Next, in step S309, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the learning region number i is n+1. As shown in fig. 6, n is the total number of learning regions determined in advance.

If it is determined in step S309 that the learning region number i is n+1, the present control routine ends. The training data set in each learning area and the prediction result during the parking are repeatedly updated by the control routine of fig. 7 and 8. Thus, in the following control routine, the allocation of the learning region is restarted from the beginning.

On the other hand, when it is determined in step S309 that the learning region number i is n or less, the present control routine proceeds to step S310. In step S310, the learning planning unit 81 sets the parking period number p to 1. After step S310, the present control routine returns to step S302 to determine whether or not the next learning region can be allocated.

In addition, when it is determined in step S303 that the parking time STp during the p-th parking period is smaller than the learning time LTi of the i-th learning region, the present control routine proceeds to step S306. In step S306, the learning planning unit 81 adds 1 to the parking period number in order to search for another parking period to which the i-th learning region can be allocated.

Next, in step S307, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the parking period number p is m+1.m is the total number of predicted parking periods, 7 in the example of fig. 5. When it is determined in step S307 that the parking period number p is m or less, the present control routine returns to step S303 to determine whether or not allocation to the next parking period is possible.

On the other hand, if it is determined in step S307 that the parking period number p is m+1, since there is no parking period in which the i-th learning region can be allocated, 1 is added to the learning region number i in step S308.

Next, in step S309, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the learning region number i is n+1. When it is determined that the learning region number i is n+1, the present control routine ends. On the other hand, when it is determined that the learning region number i is n or less, the present control routine proceeds to step S310, and the subsequent processing is the processing described above.

As described above, in the present control routine, it is determined whether or not allocation is possible in order from the learning region having the small learning region number i. As a result, the learning region having the relatively small learning region number i is preferentially allocated to the parking period than the learning region having the relatively large learning region number i. That is, in the present embodiment, the learning region number i indicates the priority of learning, and the smaller the learning region number i is, the higher the priority of learning in the learning region is. Therefore, it can be said that a priority of learning is given to a plurality of learning regions. In the example of fig. 6, the priority is given in the order of arrangement of the learning regions, but the priority may be given at random, for example.

< learning Process >)

Fig. 10 is a flowchart showing a control routine of learning processing in the first embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the ECU 60.

First, in step S401, the learning unit 83 determines whether or not the vehicle is currently parked. For example, the learning unit 83 determines that the vehicle is currently in the parking period when the state in which the speed of the vehicle detected by the vehicle speed sensor 77 is zero continues for a predetermined time or longer. When it is determined in step S401 that the vehicle is not currently in the parking period, that is, when it is determined that the vehicle is currently in the traveling period, the present control routine ends.

On the other hand, when it is determined in step S401 that the vehicle is currently in the parking period, the present control routine proceeds to step S402. In step S402, the learning unit 83 determines the parking period number p of the current parking period by comparing the date and time of the parking period predicted by the parking period predicting unit 84 with the current date and time.

Next, in step S402, the learning unit 83 determines whether or not a learning area is allocated to the parking period of the parking period number p determined in step S402. When it is determined that the learning region is not allocated, the present control routine ends. On the other hand, when it is determined that the learning region is allocated, the present control routine advances to step S404.

In step S404, the learning unit 83 learns the neural network model in the assigned learning region. Specifically, the learning unit 83 repeatedly updates the weights w and the values of the offsets b in the neural network model by the error back propagation method described above using the training data set in the assigned learning region. After step S404, the present control routine ends.

The learning unit 83 updates the neural network model after completion of learning. Specifically, the learning unit 83 changes the values of the weight w and the bias b in the neural network model to the final values updated by learning. The computing unit 85 calculates the output parameters using the updated neural network model.

< second embodiment >

The machine learning device according to the second embodiment is basically the same as the machine learning device according to the first embodiment in its configuration and control except for the points described below. Therefore, the second embodiment of the present invention will be described below mainly with respect to the differences from the first embodiment.

In the first embodiment, the plurality of learning regions are defined by combinations of different ranges of the input parameters, respectively. On the other hand, in the second embodiment, the plurality of learning regions includes a small learning region and a large learning region including the small learning region. The small learning region and the large learning region are determined such that the data density of the small learning region is higher than the data density of the large learning region. That is, the small learning region is defined by a range of input parameters having a relatively high frequency of occurrence, and the difference region between the large learning region and the small learning region is defined by a range of input parameters having a relatively low frequency of occurrence.

The learning section 83 selectively assigns a small learning region and a large learning region to the parking period. In this case, the training data set in the small learning region is always used in learning of the neural network model. Therefore, learning of the neural network model can be facilitated with respect to a range of input parameters whose frequency of occurrence is relatively high. As a result, the accuracy of calculating the output parameter by the neural network model in a typical running state of the vehicle can be improved.

Fig. 11 schematically shows a plurality of learning regions in the second embodiment. In this example, the 2 nd learning region (i=2) includes the 1 st learning region (i=1), and the 3 rd learning region (i=3) includes the 1 st learning region (i=1) and the 2 nd learning region (i=2). Therefore, the 1 st learning region corresponds to the small learning region, and the 2 nd learning region and the 3 rd learning region correspond to the large learning region. The number of large learning regions may be other than 2.

For example, the small learning region and the large learning region are predetermined such that the data density of the small learning region is higher than the data density of the large learning region based on the prediction of the occurrence frequency of the range of each of the plurality of input parameters. The small learning region and the large learning region may be determined such that the data density of the small learning region is higher than the data density of the large learning region based on the actual measurement value of the input parameter acquired in a predetermined period after the vehicle leaves the factory.

< learning plan creation Process >)

In the second embodiment, the control routine of fig. 12 is executed instead of the control routine of fig. 9, in addition to the control routines of fig. 7, 8, and 10. Fig. 12 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the learning plan creation process in the second embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the ECU60 at predetermined time intervals.

First, in step S501, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not a training data set exists in the i-th learning region, as in step S301 of fig. 9. The initial value of the learning region number i is 1. If it is determined that the training data set does not exist in the i-th learning region, the present control routine ends. On the other hand, when it is determined that the training data set exists in the i-th learning region, the present control routine proceeds to step S502. Since the 2 nd learning region and the 3 rd learning region include the 1 st learning region, when the training data set exists in the 1 st learning region, the training data set also exists in the 2 nd learning region and the 3 rd learning region.

In step S502, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the parking time STp during the p-th parking is equal to or longer than the learning time LT3 of the 3 rd learning region. At this time, the learning planning unit 81 calculates the learning time LT3 of the 3 rd learning region based on the number of training data sets divided into the 3 rd learning region. The greater the number of training data sets, the longer the learning time LT3 of the 3 rd learning region. On the other hand, as the parking time STp in the p-th parking period, a value predicted by the parking period predicting unit 84 may be used. The initial value of the parking period number p is 1.

When it is determined in step S502 that the parking time STp during the p-th parking period is not less than the learning time LT3 of the 3 rd learning region, the present control routine proceeds to step S503. In step S503, the learning planning unit 81 allocates the 3 rd learning region to the p-th parking period.

Next, in step S508, the learning planning unit 81 adds 1 to the parking period number p in order to determine whether or not allocation to the next parking period is possible. Next, in step S509, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the parking period number p is m+1.m is the total number of predicted parking periods.

When it is determined in step S509 that the parking period number p is m or less, the present control routine ends. On the other hand, when it is determined in step S509 that the parking period number p is m+1, the present control routine proceeds to step S510. In step S510, the learning planning unit 81 resets the parking period number p to 1 (initial value). After step S510, the present control routine ends.

In addition, when it is determined in step S502 that the parking time STp during the p-th parking period is smaller than the learning time LT3 of the 3 rd learning region, the present control routine proceeds to step S504. In step S504, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the parking time STp during p-parking is equal to or longer than the learning time LT2 of the 2 nd learning region. At this time, the learning planning unit 81 calculates the learning time LT2 of the 2 nd learning region based on the number of training data sets assigned to the 2 nd learning region. The greater the number of training data sets, the longer the learning time LT2 of the 2 nd learning region. Further, since the 3 rd learning region includes the 2 nd learning region, the learning time LT2 of the 2 nd learning region is not more than the learning time LT3 of the 3 rd learning region.

When it is determined in step S504 that the parking time STp during the p-th parking period is not less than the learning time LT2 of the 2 nd learning region, the present control routine proceeds to step S505. In step S505, the learning planning unit 81 allocates the 2 nd learning region to the p-th parking period. Next, step S508 to step S510 are executed as described above.

On the other hand, when it is determined in step S504 that the parking time STp during the p-th parking is smaller than the learning time LT2 of the 2 nd learning region, the present control routine proceeds to step S506. In step S506, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the parking time STp during p parking is equal to or longer than the learning time LT1 of the 1 st learning region. At this time, the learning planning unit 81 calculates the learning time LT1 of the 1 st learning region based on the number of training data sets assigned to the 1 st learning region. The greater the number of training data sets, the longer the learning time LT1 of the 1 st learning region. Since the 3 rd learning region and the 2 nd learning region include the 1 st learning region, the learning time LT1 of the 1 st learning region is equal to or less than the learning time LT3 of the 3 rd learning region and the learning time LT2 of the 2 nd learning region.

If it is determined in step S506 that the parking time STp during the p-th parking period is equal to or longer than the learning time LT1 of the 1 st learning region, the control routine proceeds to step S507. In step S507, the learning planning unit 81 allocates the 1 st learning region to the p-th parking period. Next, step S508 to step S510 are executed as described above.

On the other hand, when it is determined in step S506 that the parking time STp during the p-th parking period is smaller than the learning time LT1 of the 1 st learning region, the present control routine proceeds to step S508, and steps S508 to S510 are executed as described above.

< third embodiment >

The machine learning device according to the third embodiment is basically the same as the machine learning device according to the first embodiment in its configuration and control except for the points described below. Therefore, the third embodiment of the present invention will be described mainly with respect to the differences from the first embodiment.

In the third embodiment, a priority of learning is given to a plurality of learning regions as in the first embodiment. On the other hand, in the third embodiment, unlike the first embodiment, the learning planning section 81 makes the priority of learning of the learning region including the value of the input parameter having a relatively high frequency of occurrence higher than the priority of learning of the learning region including the value of the input parameter having a relatively low frequency of occurrence. Therefore, learning of the neural network model can be facilitated with respect to a range of input parameters whose frequency of occurrence is relatively high. As a result, the accuracy of calculating the output parameter by the neural network model in a typical running state of the vehicle can be improved.

In the third embodiment, a space defined by a plurality of input parameters is divided into a plurality of initial areas. The plurality of initial regions are divided into three learning regions (a 1 st learning region, a 2 nd learning region, and a 3 rd learning region) based on the number of times of acquisition of actual measurement values of input parameters acquired in the vehicle. The initial region is the same region as the learning region shown in fig. 5. In the third embodiment, the number of learning regions may be any number of two or more.

In the third embodiment, the control routine of fig. 7 to 10 is executed as in the first embodiment. At this time, in the third embodiment, in step S103 of fig. 7, the data set creating unit 82 divides the training data set into the learning region and the initial region. In this case, the training data set is stored in the memory 62 of the ECU60 together with the learning region number i of the corresponding learning region and the initial region number q of the corresponding initial region.

< learning region setting Process >)

In the third embodiment, the control routine of fig. 13 is executed in addition to the control routines of fig. 7 to 10. Fig. 13 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the learning region setting process in the third embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the ECU60 at predetermined time intervals.

First, in step S601, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the number Nq of training data sets divided into the q-th initial region is equal to or greater than the 1 st reference value R1. The 1 st reference value R1 is predetermined. The initial value of the initial region number q is 1.

When it is determined in step S601 that the number Nq of training data sets is equal to or greater than the 1 st reference value R1, the present control routine proceeds to step S602. In step S602, the learning planning unit 81 sets the learning region number i of the q-th initial region to 1.

Next, in step S607, the learning planning unit 81 adds 1 to the initial region number q in order to set the learning region number i of the next initial region. Next, in step S608, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the initial region number q is k+1.k is the total number of predetermined initial regions.

When it is determined in step S608 that the initial area number q is k or less, the present control routine ends. On the other hand, when it is determined in step S608 that the initial area number q is k+1, the present control routine proceeds to step S609. In step S609, the learning planning unit 81 resets the initial region number q to 1 (initial value). After step S609, the present control routine ends.

On the other hand, when it is determined in step S601 that the number Nq of training data sets is smaller than the 1 st reference value R1, the present control routine proceeds to step S603. In step S603, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the number Nq of training data sets divided into the q-th initial region is equal to or greater than the 2 nd reference value R2. The 2 nd reference value R2 is predetermined and set to a value smaller than the 1 st reference value R1.

If it is determined in step S603 that the number Nq of training data sets is equal to or greater than the 2 nd reference value R2, the present control routine proceeds to step S604. In step S604, the learning planning unit 81 sets the learning region number i of the q-th initial region to 2. In the control routine of fig. 9, the 1 st learning region is assigned to the parking period preferentially over the 2 nd learning region. Therefore, the priority of learning in the 2 nd learning region is lower than the priority of learning in the 1 st learning region. Next, step S607 to step S609 are executed as described above.

On the other hand, when it is determined in step S603 that the number Nq of training data sets is smaller than the 2 nd reference value R2, the present control routine proceeds to step S605. In step S605, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the number Nq of training data sets divided into the q-th initial region is equal to or greater than the 3 rd reference value R3. The 3 rd reference value R3 is predetermined and set to a value smaller than the 1 st reference value R1 and the 2 nd reference value R2.

When it is determined in step S605 that the number Nq of training data sets is equal to or greater than the 3 rd reference value R3, the present control routine proceeds to step S606. In step S606, the learning planning unit 81 sets the learning region number i of the q-th initial region to 3. In the control routine of fig. 9, the 1 st learning region and the 2 nd learning region are assigned to the parking period preferentially over the 3 rd learning region. Therefore, the learning priority of the 3 rd learning region is lower than the learning priorities of the 1 st learning region and the 2 nd learning region. Next, step S607 to step S609 are executed as described above.

< fourth embodiment >, a third embodiment

The machine learning device according to the fourth embodiment is basically the same as the machine learning device according to the first embodiment in its configuration and control except for the points described below. Therefore, the fourth embodiment of the present invention will be described mainly with respect to the differences from the first embodiment.

In the fourth embodiment, the learning unit 83 learns a plurality of neural network models. The neural network models output different kinds of output parameters respectively.

For example, the learning unit 83 learns six neural network models. For example, in the 1 st neural network model, the input parameters include the engine speed, the fresh air amount, and the ignition timing, and the output parameters include the Hydrocarbon (HC) concentration in the exhaust gas. In addition, in the 2 nd neural network model, the input parameters include the engine speed, the fresh air amount, and the EGR gas amount, and the output parameters include the NOx concentration in the exhaust gas. In addition, in the 3 rd neural network model, the input parameters include the engine speed, the fresh air amount, the EGR amount, and the ignition timing, and the output parameters include the carbon monoxide (CO) concentration in the exhaust gas. In addition, in the 4 th neural network model, the input parameters include engine speed, fresh air The amount and the fuel injection amount, and the output parameter includes fuel economy of the vehicle. In addition, in the 5 th neural network model, the input parameters include the engine speed, the fresh air amount, and the ignition timing, and the output parameters include the output torque of the internal combustion engine 1. In addition, in the 6 th neural network model, the input parameters include the engine speed, the fresh air amount, and the fuel injection amount, and the output parameters include carbon dioxide (CO) in the exhaust gas 2 ) Concentration.

In this case, the actual measurement values of the input parameter and the output parameter can be obtained as follows. The engine speed is calculated based on the output of the crank angle sensor 74. The fresh air amount is detected by the air flow meter 71. The ignition timing is calculated based on a command value from the ECU60 to the spark plug. The EGR gas amount is calculated based on the opening degree of the EGR control valve 15, etc. The fuel injection amount is calculated based on a command value from the ECU60 to the fuel injection valve. The NOx concentration in the exhaust gas is detected by the NOx sensor 73. The fuel economy of a vehicle is calculated by dividing the travel distance by the fuel consumption, for example. The HC concentration, CO concentration, and CO2 concentration in the exhaust gas are calculated based on, for example, the output of the air-fuel ratio sensor 72. Further, these concentrations may also be directly detected by an exhaust gas sensor that detects the concentration of a predetermined component.

In the fourth embodiment, for each of a plurality of neural network models, a space defined by a plurality of input parameters is divided into a plurality of learning regions. Different learning area numbers are assigned to different learning areas of the neural network model. In addition, as in the first embodiment, a priority of learning is given to a plurality of learning regions.

When a plurality of neural network models that output different output parameters are learned, the priority of learning of the neural network models changes according to information of a road on which the vehicle is traveling, or the like. Therefore, the learning planning unit 81 changes the priority of learning given to the plurality of learning regions based on the information of the road on which the vehicle is traveling. This makes it possible to adapt the neural network model to the running state of the vehicle.

For example, when the road on which the vehicle is traveling is an upward slope, power required for the upward slope needs to be generated by the internal combustion engine 1. Therefore, in order to improve the accuracy of calculating the output torque of the internal combustion engine 1, the priority of learning of the neural network model (5 th neural network model) that outputs the output torque of the internal combustion engine 1 is highest.

Then, when the road on which the vehicle travels is an upward slope, the learning planning unit 81 increases the priority of the learning region corresponding to the 5 th neural network model as compared with the case where the road on which the vehicle travels is not an upward slope.

< learning region number Change Process >)

In the fourth embodiment, the control routine of fig. 14 is executed in addition to the control routines of fig. 7 to 10. Fig. 14 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the learning region number change process in the fourth embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the ECU60 at predetermined time intervals.

First, in step S801, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the road on which the vehicle is traveling is an upward slope. For example, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the road on which the vehicle is traveling is an upward slope based on the current position of the vehicle detected by the GPS receiver 92 and the map information stored in the map database 93.

In the case where it is determined in step S801 that the road on which the vehicle is traveling is not an ascending slope, the present control routine proceeds to step S803. In step S803, the learning planning unit 81 initializes the learning region number i. That is, the learning region numbers i of all the learning regions are set to predetermined initial values. After step S803, the present control routine ends.

On the other hand, when it is determined in step S801 that the road is an upward slope, the present control routine proceeds to step S802. In step S802, the learning planning unit 81 changes the learning region number i from the initial value. Specifically, the learning planning unit 81 reduces the learning region number i of the learning region corresponding to the 5 th neural network model that outputs the output torque of the internal combustion engine 1. For example, the learning region number i of the corresponding learning region is reduced in the order of the 6 th neural network model, the 4 th neural network model, the 3 rd neural network model, the 1 st neural network model, the 2 nd neural network model, and the 5 th neural network model. After step S802, the present control routine ends.

In addition, in the case where the vehicle is traveling on an expressway, the frequency of occurrence of the speed of the vehicle in a predetermined range (for example, 80km/h to 120 km/h) becomes high. Therefore, the learning planning unit 81 may increase the priority of the learning region including the vehicle speed in the predetermined range, in the case where the road on which the vehicle travels is the expressway, as compared with the case where the road on which the vehicle travels is not the expressway. In this case, the learning unit 83 performs learning of the neural network model including the speed of the vehicle as the input parameter. In this case, the learning unit 83 may learn only one neural network model.

< fifth embodiment >, a third embodiment

The machine learning device according to the fifth embodiment is basically the same as the machine learning device according to the fourth embodiment in its configuration and control except for the points described below. Therefore, the fifth embodiment of the present invention will be mainly described below with respect to the differences from the fourth embodiment.

When the neural network model is learned for the internal combustion engine 1 and a plurality of neural network models that output different output parameters as in the fourth embodiment, the priority of the learning of the neural network model changes according to the warm-up state of the internal combustion engine 1. Therefore, the learning planning unit 81 changes the priority of learning given to the plurality of learning regions based on the warm-up state of the internal combustion engine 1. This makes it possible to adapt the neural network model to the state of the internal combustion engine 1.

In the case where the warm-up of the internal combustion engine 1 is not completed, the purification performance of the catalyst 29 is low. Therefore, in order to suppress deterioration of exhaust emission, it is necessary to improve the accuracy of calculating the concentration of harmful substances (NOx, HC, and CO) in the exhaust gas. On the other hand, when the warm-up of the internal combustion engine 1 is completed, the fuel economy of the vehicle is prioritized. Therefore, when the warm-up of the internal combustion engine 1 is not completed, the learning planning unit 81 increases the priority of the learning region corresponding to the neural network model (1 st to 3 rd neural network models) that outputs the concentration of the harmful substance in the exhaust gas, and decreases the priority of the learning region corresponding to the neural network model (4 th neural network model) that outputs the fuel economy of the vehicle, as compared with the case where the warm-up of the internal combustion engine 1 is completed.

< learning region number Change Process >)

In the fifth embodiment, the control routine of fig. 15 is executed in addition to the control routines of fig. 7 to 10. Fig. 15 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the learning region number change process in the fifth embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the ECU60 at predetermined time intervals.

First, in step S901, the learning planning unit 81 obtains a warmed-up state of the internal combustion engine 1. Specifically, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the warm-up of the internal combustion engine 1 is completed. This determination is made, for example, based on the output of a water temperature sensor provided in the internal combustion engine 1, the output of an exhaust temperature sensor provided in the exhaust passage of the internal combustion engine 1, the integrated fresh air amount calculated from the output of the air flow meter 71, and the like.

Next, in step S902, the learning planning unit 81 changes the learning region number i. Specifically, when the warm-up of the internal combustion engine 1 is not completed, the learning planning unit 81 reduces the learning region number i of the learning region corresponding to the 1 st to 3 rd neural network models that output the concentration of the harmful substance in the exhaust gas, and increases the learning region number i of the learning region corresponding to the 4 th neural network model that outputs the fuel economy of the vehicle, as compared with the case where the warm-up of the internal combustion engine 1 is completed.

For example, in the case where the warm-up of the internal combustion engine 1 is not completed, the learning region number i of the corresponding learning region is reduced in the order of the 6 th neural network model, the 5 th neural network model, the 4 th neural network model, the 3 rd neural network model, the 2 nd neural network model, and the 1 st neural network model. On the other hand, when the warm-up of the internal combustion engine 1 is completed, the learning region number i of the corresponding learning region is reduced in the order of the 6 th neural network model, the 5 th neural network model, the 3 rd neural network model, the 1 st neural network model, the 2 nd neural network model, and the 4 th neural network model. After step S902, the present control routine ends.
